title: The Terrier at the Gate
subtitle: 50 words · one story
paragraphs: Bracken Lane was situated at the edge of town, past the last row of houses and a field where the grass had gone to hay. The shelter was a low brick building with a new extension on the east side, its skeleton of steel beams still open to the sky. Tomas, an undergraduate on a summer placement, had been given one simple task: organize the kennels before the inspection at nine. He was reluctant to admit that he had never held a dog before, and the technician, Nuala, had guessed it within a minute. At seven a police car stopped at the gate, and the cop carried in a terrier wrapped in a blanket.

The terrier had no chip under the skin and no collar, only a strip of rope tied in a knot. Nuala ran the scanner twice, said nothing, and wrote the word unknown on the form. She had an obligation to keep the dog for seven days, and a full list already; tomorrow morning the old dog Biscuit, beloved by every volunteer, was booked for surgery on a bad hip. The terrier, whose appearance suggested a decent family somewhere, turned out to be a nightmare on a lead. It had failed every obedience class the town could offer, and its resemblance to a dog from a lost poster made Tomas grab his phone.

The inspection was never only about clean floors, because a town election in three weeks had made every grant a matter of public argument. The council official who would arrive at nine had spent the summer under pressure from neighbours who oppose the new extension, and a spokesman for the shelter had already answered two rounds of negative questions from the local paper. Gossip moved faster than any letter: by eight o'clock half the town believed the place was closing. Nuala had no patience for persuasion and less for rumour, but she knew that a widespread story, once printed, was hard to confront with facts.

At half past eight the volunteers began to set out the open day: a paper bowl of punch on a folding table, a rack of second-hand leads by the door, and a costume parade for anyone who wanted to dress a dog as a bee. Tomas was descending the narrow stairs with an armful of bowls when he missed the last step, and a jug of punch split at the seam as the water purifier in the corner chose that moment to fail. Nuala did not shout, which was worse, because she only said that a small accident could compound a large one. Perfection was not the essence of the job, she told him, but tidiness was a privilege the shelter could not lose before nine.

At nine the official walked the whole site and found nothing to complain about, and the terrier's owner arrived at ten with a photograph and a sensible explanation of how the gate had been left open. The open day raised a gross total of four hundred pounds, which Nuala said would pay for a month of food. That evening Tomas wrote a comprehensive report, and in it he confessed that one illustration on their leaflet could mislead a nervous reader; the drawing showed a dog in a cage, and the shelter had none. Nuala read it twice, and her acceptance of the mistake was, he thought, more useful than praise. Undoubtedly the work had matured him, and on reflection his outlook on it had changed as well.
translations: 布拉肯巷坐落于小镇边缘，过了最后一排房子，是一片草已长成干草的田。收容所是一栋低矮的砖房，东侧新加了一截扩建，钢梁骨架还敞在天空底下。托马斯是来做暑期实习的本科生，只领到一个简单任务：九点检查之前把犬舍理好。他不愿承认自己从没抱过狗，可技术员努阿拉一分钟就看了出来。七点，一辆警车停在门口，警察抱进来一只裹在毯子里的梗犬。
那只梗犬皮下没有芯片，也没有项圈，只有一截打了结的绳子。努阿拉扫了两遍扫描仪，什么也没说，在表格上写下「不明」。她有义务把狗留上七天，而手上的名单已经排满；明天早上，人人喜欢的老狗「饼干」要为坏掉的一条髋关节做手术。那梗犬的外表说明它本来有个像样的家，牵在绳上却成了噩梦。镇上能开的服从课它全上遍了，一门没过；它跟一张寻狗启事上的狗长得极像，托马斯因此抓起了手机。
这场检查从来不只是地板干不干净，因为三周后的镇选举已经让每一笔拨款都成了公开争论的题目。九点要来那位市政官员，整个夏天都顶着反对新扩建的邻居的压力；收容所的发言人已经应付过本地报纸两轮负面提问。闲话比信件快得多：到八点，半个镇子都相信这地方要关门了。努阿拉没耐心去说服谁，更没耐心听传言，可她知道，一个传得广的说法一旦上了报，就很难拿事实去面对。
八点半，志愿者开始铺开开放日的场面：折叠桌上一碗潘趣酒，门边一排二手牵引绳，还有一场给狗扮成蜜蜂的变装游行。托马斯抱着一摞碗下窄楼梯，踩空了最后一级，一罐潘趣酒顺着接缝裂开，角落里那台净水器偏偏在这时坏了。努阿拉没有喊，这反而更糟，因为她只说了一句：小事故会让大问题更严重。她告诉他，完美不是这份工作的本质，但整洁是收容所在九点之前丢不起的特权。
九点，那位官员走遍全场，没挑出什么毛病；十点，梗犬的主人带着一张照片来了，把门是怎么被留开的解释得很在理。开放日一共募到四百英镑的总额，努阿拉说够买一个月的粮。当晚托马斯写了一份全面的报告，在里面承认他们传单上的一幅插图可能误导紧张的读者：画上是一只关在笼子里的狗，而这里根本没有笼子。努阿拉读了两遍，他觉得，她接受这个错误，比表扬他更有用。这份工作无疑让他成熟了，回头一想，他对它的看法也变了。

sense_map.comprehensive: adj. 全面的（一份全面的报告）
sense_map.obedience: n. 服从（obedience class 指服从训练课）
sense_map.nightmare: n. 很难对付的人或事
sense_map.purify: v. 净化（文中 purifier 指净水器）
sense_map.situate: v. 使坐落于（situated 坐落于）
sense_map.reflection: n. 深思（on reflection 回头一想）
sense_map.punch: n. 潘趣酒（果汁加汽水调成的饮品）

situate: was situated at the edge of town
undergraduate: an undergraduate on a summer placement
privilege: a privilege the shelter could not lose
obligation: an obligation to keep the dog

gone to hay.usage: go to + 名词表示「变成某种状态」，农田 go to hay 指弃耕长草；hay 是不可数名词，不加 s

skeleton of steel beams.usage: skeleton 指支撑整体的骨架，of 后接构成材料；建筑封顶前常说 the skeleton is up

reluctant to admit.usage: reluctant 后接 to do，语气比 unwilling 委婉，多指心里不情愿而非明确拒绝

an obligation to keep.usage: obligation to do sth 指道义或法律上的义务；正式文里常用 under an obligation to

beloved by every volunteer.usage: beloved 多作定语，或用于 be beloved of / by sb.，比 loved 文气，常用于人或宠物

a nightmare on a lead.usage: nightmare 可指极难对付的人或事；on a lead 指拴着牵引绳，英国说法，美国多用 on a leash

under pressure from.usage: under pressure from sb 指受某人施压；press 作动词常写 pressure sb into doing sth

a spokesman for the shelter.usage: spokesman for + 机构；女性用 spokeswoman，性别不明用 spokesperson，介词一律用 for

confront with facts.usage: confront sb with sth 是拿某事与人对质；confront sth with sth 则是正面应对，如用事实应对传言

a rack of second-hand leads.usage: rack 指挂放物品的架子，of 后接所挂之物；rack 作动词另有「使受折磨」义

could compound a large one.usage: compound 作动词指使问题加重，常与 problem / difficulty / error 搭配，不用于人

the essence of the job.usage: the essence of + 名词指核心要义；固定短语 in essence 意为「本质上」

a gross total of.usage: gross 作形容词指未扣除前的总额，gross income / gross weight；与 net 相对

could mislead a nervous reader.usage: mislead 指使人形成错误判断，常用 mislead sb into doing sth；名词形式是 misleading

on reflection.usage: on / upon reflection 表示经过思考后修正先前的判断，多置于句首或句末
